title: Concept record
description: One teachable concept. The atomic unit of the course. Authored once, assembled into per-subject booklets and, later, into interleaving problem sets. Field order here is the order the fields are authored in.

concept_id.description: Permanent identifier, never reused and never renumbered even if the concept moves position. Form: SUBJECT-RUNG-CONCEPT, e.g. S01-R1-C03. Book 0 concepts use B0-R0-Cnn. Interleaving problems reference concepts by this ID, so a change here silently breaks a problem set.

subject.description: Subject ID from the frozen v3 map, or B0 for Book 0.

rung.description: Rung number within the subject. 0 is reserved for Book 0 ground-floor material, which belongs to no rung.

sequence.description: Teaching order within the rung. Contiguous, and re-orderable without touching concept_id.

name.description: Short noun phrase, as it appears as a section heading.

concept_type.description: Governs the sourcing rule, the treatment and the review clock. derivable: can be built from the reader floor by argument; anchor to a canonical text. empirical: cannot be derived, must be asserted with evidence; cite the primary study or a named systematic review, and state what would overturn it. institutional: true because a body decided it; cite the instrument itself and stamp an as-of date.

clusters.description: Thematic cluster keys from clusters.yml. Drives composition of the interleaving problem sets. A concept may sit in more than one.

ground_floor_deps.description: Book 0 concepts this concept requires. Determines what the booklet's micro-refresher must cover and is checked by the build.

concept_deps.description: Other concept records assumed by this one. Within a subject these must be at the same or a lower rung; the build fails on a forward reference, which is what enforces the unbroken chain.

definition.description: Technically accurate statement of the concept. Mandatory for every concept.

text.description: The definition. Precise enough to survive a specialist reading it; no hedging, no simplification. Simplification belongs in the next field.

kind.description: Must be consistent with concept_type: derivable takes textbook; empirical takes primary or systematic_review; institutional takes instrument, guideline or consensus_statement.

locator.description: Page, section, clause or table where the claim is actually located. Not optional: this is what makes the citation checkable.

resolved_id.description: DOI, ISBN, statute number or stable URL.

opened.description: The source was obtained and read. Never set true without doing so.

claim_located.description: The specific claim was found at the locator.

note.description: Used when a source could not be obtained, or when it says something subtly different from the claim.

quote_checked.description: Set by the build, not by hand: the quote was found in the source file.

quote.description: The exact words from the source that carry this claim, copied not paraphrased. When the source is a file in sources/, the build searches that file for this string and blocks if it is not there. This is the only field that makes a citation checkable by machine.

simplified_explanation.description: The same concept rebuilt from the reader floor, assuming no medicine and no remembered mathematics. Mandatory for every concept. Permitted to be loose where the definition is exact; not permitted to be wrong.

illustration.description: Worked example, case, calculation or analogy. Mandatory for every concept. Indian context wherever the concept has Indian specificity; see STYLE.md.

analogy_breaks_when.description: The point at which this illustration stops being true. Required, including for numerical examples, where it states the range of validity. An illustration without a stated failure boundary teaches a misconception with the concept.

numbers.description: Every quoted figure, so the numbers register can check it without re-reading prose.

quote.description: The words in the source that state this number. Checked against sources/.

derived.description: For a number counted or derived from the quoted words rather than stated in them: say how. Reported, never silent.

must_know.description: Must-know points for the reader. Mandatory for every concept; the number varies with what the concept demands, not with a template. Rendered under the heading 'Must know points for you'. Admission test: the point must change something the reader would do, say, accept or refuse as the expert this course is building. A true, interesting statement that changes nothing belongs in the illustration or in nothing.

point.description: One point, one paragraph, written so the consequence is inside it. Not a heading with the content implied.

bearing.description: Which capacity of the expert this point arms. clinical: changes what you do or say in front of a patient. methodological: changes what you accept as evidence, or how you design or critique a study. policy: changes what you say in a consultation, committee or testimony. teaching: changes what you teach or how you correct a trainee. public: changes what you say to a journalist or in public. The build tallies these so a corpus tilted entirely one way is visible.

kind.description: Optional tag, for the author's discipline and for composing revision sets. misconception: the error a reader is most likely to make, stated as the error. number: a figure worth holding in your head, with unit and source. india_deviation: how this differs in India, or the explicit statement that it does not. boundary: what this does not cover, so it is not over-applied. trap: the viva, reviewer or journalist question that catches someone who half-knows this. consequence: what follows in practice. dispute: what is genuinely contested, and by whom. move: a concrete thing to do, in the order to do it. The build warns when a concept has no misconception and no trap.

refs.description: Citekeys, where the point carries a figure or an institutional fact that needs one.

exercises.description: Present where the rung's skills or build target require practice. Optional at concept level; the rung as a whole must cover all its skills. Type taxonomy is fixed in STYLE.md.

type.description: integrative is reserved for the interleaving booklets and is not authored inside a subject booklet.

answer.description: Worked reasoning, not just the result. Rendered to the booklet appendix, never beside the prompt.

skill_ref.description: The rung skill from v3 this exercise demonstrates, so skill coverage can be checked mechanically.

confidence_first.description: If true, the reader is asked to record a numerical confidence before revealing the answer. Trains S59 calibration.

quantitative.description: True where the concept teaches a mathematical technique the reader has to be able to carry out, rather than a fact or a distinction they have to be able to state. A quantitative concept carries a ten-problem practice set; the build blocks without one. Omitted, it is derived: a Book 0 record in Part A, B, C or D is quantitative, everything else is not. Set it explicitly on a subject record whose rung teaches a calculation, and set it explicitly to false on a Book 0 record in a mathematical Part that genuinely teaches no technique.

practice.description: The drill set. Exactly ten problems on one technique, in ascending difficulty, mandatory for every quantitative concept. Distinct from `exercises`, which carry the rung's skills and build target and use the fixed type taxonomy; these carry fluency in the technique and nothing else. Prompts print in the section, unsolved and in order; answers print in the booklet appendix, never beside the prompt. Full rule in STYLE.md 7a.

level.description: Position on the difficulty ladder. The ten levels in a set are 1 to 10, each used exactly once, and the build blocks otherwise: this is what makes 'progressive' checkable rather than a matter of taste. 1-3 mechanical, on bare numbers. 4-6 applied, on a real quantity with its unit and label. 7-8 diagnostic, on a worked answer that is wrong. 9-10 transfer, on a claim in words where the reader must choose the technique and say what the answer does not establish.

prompt.description: What the reader is to do. Unsolved. Carries no hint of the answer and no worked fragment.

answer.description: Every line of the working, not just the result, per STYLE.md 4. Rendered to the appendix.

refs.description: Citekeys, where the problem quotes a real figure. Checked against library.bib exactly as must_know refs are, so a drill built on an invented statistic fails the build.

retrieval_items.description: Two or three question-answer pairs per concept, emitted for a spaced-repetition system. Authored while writing, because extracting them later means re-reading everything.

provenance.description: Ties the concept back to the frozen map. The map states outcomes; this record is part of how a reader reaches them.

map_version_id.description: Version id of the frozen subject map this was derived against.

outcome_refs.description: Which rung outcome statements, skills or gate this concept serves. A concept serving none is out of scope.

bridge_ref.description: Which Intermediate-rung presuppositions this concept discharges. Populated by the bridge-sufficiency test.

review.description: The review clock. Falls out of concept_type and is what lets the build report expired content.

stability.description: long: derivable, five-yearly. medium: empirical, two to three years. short: institutional, event-driven.

trigger.description: For long and medium, a date. For short, the event: 'next FSSAI notification', 'next GST Council revision', 'next NFHS round', 'next ICMR-NIN RDA revision'.

as_of.description: Date the content was true. Mandatory for institutional concepts; printed in the booklet.

status.description: stub: generated spine only. drafted: prose written. referenced: citations attached. verified: citations opened and claims located. released: published in a booklet edition.

illustrations.description: Two or more illustrations, where one does not do the teaching. Use instead of 'illustration', not alongside it.

items.description: Worked example, case, calculation or analogy. Mandatory for every concept. Indian context wherever the concept has Indian specificity; see STYLE.md.

analogy_breaks_when.description: The point at which this illustration stops being true. Required, including for numerical examples, where it states the range of validity. An illustration without a stated failure boundary teaches a misconception with the concept.

numbers.description: Every quoted figure, so the numbers register can check it without re-reading prose.

quote.description: The words in the source that state this number. Checked against sources/.

derived.description: For a number counted or derived from the quoted words rather than stated in them: say how. Reported, never silent.

figures.description: Figures generated into check/figures/ and embedded at build time. A figure earns its place only when it shows something the prose cannot say in the same space; 'source' names the script that draws it, so the picture and the numbers behind it cannot drift apart unnoticed.

source.description: Script under check/figures/ that draws it.

spec.description: The figure's data, the only copy of it. check/figures/draw.py --book <ID> draws the figure from this in the book's colours; check/build.py blocks unless every number plotted or printed (data, labels, caption, alt, axis titles, relation constants) is stated in the record's reader-facing text or worked out in `derived`, every `fit` passes through every plotted point, every `check` holds, and the PNG's .spec.json fingerprint matches. Required for every figure outside Book 0.

from_table.description: Read the data from the record's own nth ```table block (counted across its illustrations, from 0); x and y are column indexes.

marker.description: Line/step only: draw the series as a line with no point markers (for a fitted line, not observations).

fit.description: y = <expression in x>; every plotted point must satisfy it at the precision the value is written to.

check.description: An identity over the data, e.g. 'sum(y) = 91' or 'y[0] / y[-1] = 1.78'.

derived.description: A number the figure prints that the prose does not state, with the arithmetic that gives it from numbers the prose does state (names x, y, y1, y2... are the data).

bands.description: Shaded horizontal ranges drawn behind the data, e.g. a range the text gives. y0, y1 and any number in label are checked against the text like every plotted number.

figure_note.description: One line saying why no figure would teach anything this section's prose does not. Every section outside Book 0 carries a figure or this note.

practice_note.description: Why this drill set sits outside the three-to-eighteen range (STYLE.md 7a).
